brief: Goldman's Novak morning note leads with the Fed's hawkish surprise. The FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4%, with a 16-2 majority projecting another hike this year, no dissents, a higher neutral-rate dot (3.06% to 3.25%), and Warsh repeating that the hike removed a dose of accommodation. Goldman now expects a second 25bp hike in October instead of treating September as the last move, but keeps its 3.25-3.5% terminal-rate forecast by adding a third cut in March 2028, because its core PCE forecast sits below the FOMC's median for both 2026 and 2027. Futures rose 80bp pre-market led by tech. The BOE is expected to hold. POTUS floated more EU tariffs if the bloc admits Canada. On micro, Lennar missed Q3 EPS and revenue with orders down 9% and softer Q4 guidance. GFL's CEO said he would consider going private. Generac signed an AMZN supply deal with a warrant struck above the stock's close. Granite Construction's CEO outlined 10%+ 2027 organic growth from federal and data center work. A Carnival earnings preview argues near-term catalysts are missing but long-term PROPEL upside is underappreciated.
